title: Contributing Google Sheets API support to a popular open-source boilerplate
situation: Hackathon Starter is a widely used open-source Node.js boilerplate with ready-made integrations for popular APIs. At hackathons I kept needing Google Sheets as a quick database or data source, and the boilerplate had no example for it.
task: Contribute a Google Sheets API integration that met the project's conventions and that maintainers would accept.
action: I studied how existing API examples were structured (routes, controllers, views and OAuth configuration) and built the Google Sheets example to match exactly instead of adding my own patterns. I documented the setup steps for getting credentials, tested the OAuth flow end to end, and opened a pull request explaining the use case. I responded to maintainer feedback [confirm: what feedback you got, if any]. Separately, I contributed documentation to Red Hat's Agile Integration workshop on APIs and containers.
result: My Google Sheets API boilerplate was merged into Hackathon Starter, where other developers can use it [confirm: merged]. What I learned: in open source, matching the project's existing conventions matters more than clever code. Maintainers merge what's easy to review and maintain.
